m:stare: The square and the Barbican can be seen for free, at any hour. On the square is the Museum of Warsaw (Rynek Starego Miasta 28-42): Tuesday–Friday 10am–6pm (Thursday until 8pm), Saturday 10am–7pm, Sunday 10am–6pm, closed on Mondays; ticket 25 zł (about €5.70), reduced 18 zł, the permanent exhibition is free on Thursdays; the fifth-floor terrace costs 10 zł extra (muzea.waw.pl page, updated 11 October 2026, not the museum's official website). The museum closes on 1 November and 24–26 and 31 December 2026.
m:zamek: Open Tuesday–Sunday from 10am to 6pm, closed on Mondays (muzea.waw.pl page, updated 11 October 2026). Ticket for the Royal Route and the Museum Route: 60 zł (about €13.70), reduced 45 zł. On Wednesdays entry is free only to some areas (the Palace under the Copper Roof and a special route): the other rooms are closed. In November 2026 there's a free route that includes the state rooms. Until December 2026 there are roof works in phases, but the castle stays open. Closed on 1 November, 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January; open on 26 December. Check zamek-krolewski.pl.
m:krakowskie: Free to walk. The Chopin Museum (Okólnik 1) has been closed for works since January 2026 and should reopen in January 2027 (muzea.waw.pl page, updated 30 September 2026): it can't be visited. I couldn't find the hours for Holy Cross Church: see the sign at the door.
m:sasski: The square and garden are outdoors and free to cross. I don't have an official source for the honour guard and changing times: see the signs on the spot.
m:pkin: The terrace costs 22 zł (about €5), reduced 15 zł (from a December 2023 article on kb.pl: the price may have changed, check on bilety.pkin.pl where you buy online). I couldn't find the terrace opening hours from an up-to-date source: check them first. Guided tours of the building start at 11am, 1, 2 and 3pm from 40 zł (pik.warszawa.pl, 2026 programme) and include the terrace without the queue.
m:powstanie: Open Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday from 8am to 6pm, Saturday and Sunday from 10am to 6pm; closed on Tuesdays, 1 November 2026, 25 December and 1 January 2027 (muzea.waw.pl page, checked 7 October 2026). Ticket 35 zł (about €8), reduced 30 zł. On Thursdays entry is free, with tickets collected at the desk on the day and long queues. The visit takes from two and a half to four hours.
m:polin: Open every day from 10am to 6pm, Saturdays until 8pm, closed on Tuesdays (muzea.waw.pl page, updated 30 September 2026). Ticket 45 zł (about €10.30), reduced 35 zł; on Thursdays entry is free. The permanent exhibition takes 3–5 hours: if you're short of time, choose the rooms from the Middle Ages to the 20th century. I found no holiday closure notices: check polin.pl.
m:lazienki: Entry to the park is free. The palaces, including the Palace on the Isle, are paid: a 2021 source gave 40 zł full and 20 zł reduced, a 2026 one mentions about 70 zł for a combined ticket to several buildings (figures not confirmed). I couldn't find the palaces' opening hours: see lazienki-krolewskie.pl. The Sunday Chopin concerts run from mid-May to the end of September, so not now.
m:wilanow: Take bus 116, 180 or 519 from the centre, 30–40 minutes (2026 guide), or a taxi in 20–30 minutes. The palace and the park have separate tickets; on Thursdays entry to the museum is free according to a guide. Hours vary with the season and I couldn't find those for October–November 2026: check wilanow-palac.pl. It's a half-day stop.
m:praga: Free to walk outdoors. Nearest M2 metro stop: Dworzec Wileński, about 10 minutes on foot. The hours of the individual venues in Koneser vary: check on the spot.
vd:familijny: One of the centre's «bar mleczny», the Polish canteens born in the communist era, on Nowy Świat street. Order at the counter and eat at shared tables: żurek with white sausage, pancakes with curd cheese (naleśniki z twarogiem), minced-meat cutlets.
vp:familijny: A dish usually costs 15–30 zł (€3.50–7), a soup less (estimate from online guides: menu not seen). Hours from tablejourney.com, to be confirmed; closed on Sundays.
vd:prasowy: A bar mleczny open since 1954 in a Socialist Realist building in the centre: home-style Polish cooking at low prices, with soups, pierogi, cutlets and sides chosen at the counter.
vp:prasowy: A soup usually costs 4–8 zł and a main course 15–30 zł (about €1–7) (estimate from online guides: menu not seen). I couldn't find the hours: the 8am–7pm shown is an estimate, to be checked.
vd:pyzy: A simple Polish place in Praga, near the Różycki market: pyzy, large potato dumplings with mushroom sauce, tripe soup (flaki) and breaded pork. Home cooking, no frills.
vp:pyzy: A dish is around 20–40 zł (€4.50–9) (estimate, menu not seen). Hours from tablejourney.com, to be confirmed.
vd:pyzystare: The Old Town branch of the same place: pyzy with mushroom sauce, flaki and breaded pork, a short walk from the Barbican. Good for a Polish lunch or dinner without paying square-restaurant prices.
vp:pyzystare: A dish is around 20–40 zł (€4.50–9) (estimate, menu not seen). I couldn't find this branch's hours: they're the Praga branch's, to be checked.
vd:wedel: The chocolate lounge of the Polish brand E. Wedel, opened in 1894, in a room with mirrors and chandeliers: thick hot chocolate, cakes and chocolates. It's a place for a sweet breakfast or afternoon snack, not a meal.
vp:wedel: A hot chocolate with a slice of cake is around 30–50 zł (€7–11) (estimate, menu not seen). Hours from inyourpocket.com, to be confirmed.
vd:koszyki: A restored early-20th-century covered market, with more than twenty stalls of Polish and world food: sandwiches, ramen, burgers, cheeses and hot dishes, and craft beer. Get food from the various stalls and sit at the shared tables.
vp:koszyki: A meal is around 30–60 zł (€7–14) depending on the stall (estimate, menu not seen). The market is normally open from 8am to 1am, but individual stalls open later or close earlier: check koszyki.com.
vd:lukullus: A family pâtisserie open since 1946, known for pączki, fried doughnuts filled with rose jam, and for its cakes. Stop at a little table or buy to eat in the street.
vp:lukullus: A pączek usually costs 6–10 zł (about €1.50–2.30) and a slice of cake 15–25 zł (estimate, menu not seen). Hours from tablejourney.com, to be confirmed.
vd:beirut: A Lebanese place on a central street full of restaurants: hummus, falafel, mezze to share, and a list of Lebanese beers and wines. It isn't Polish food, but it's a good, mid-priced dinner, open until late.
vp:beirut: A dish or a round of mezze is around 40–70 zł (€9–16) (estimate, menu not seen). According to tablejourney.com it's open until 2am; here the hours are marked until midnight, to be confirmed.
cd:museonaz: Polish and European art, from ancient Egypt to Monet.
cd:copernico: The hands-on science museum, on the Vistula riverside.
cd:curie: The scientist's birthplace, in the New Town.
cd:chopin: The composer's manuscripts and piano, in a Baroque palace.
cd:vodka: The history of vodka, with a tasting of three samples.
cd:neon: Communist-era illuminated signs, in the Soho Factory complex.
cd:zoovarsavia: A historic zoo with small enclosures and a rose garden.
cd:museovarsavia: Six Old Town houses telling the city's history.
